premise.title: Pangaea Is Overheating — Which Escape Plan Keeps You Alive? 🔥
premise.banner: The tropics turn lethal. Go where?
premise.hook_vo: Pangaea's tropics are too hot to live in.
premise.art_direction: Bleached white-gold desert glare, heat haze, hard noon shadows turning to copper dusk, ultra-wide 16mm.

options.label: Shady tropical riverbank
options.vo: Rest on a shady tropical riverbank.
options.image_prompt: Unoccupied natural-history view along a narrow muddy river in an arid Early Triassic landscape. A slow brown-green water channel curves diagonally from the lower left into the far right distance. The near riverbank is dry rust-red mineral earth with exposed brown roots and scattered stones. Two sparse drought-stressed conifers cast thin long shadows across a small patch of bare ground beside the water. Beyond them lies a pale dusty plain in heat haze. Copper sunlight enters from the upper right behind the conifers, with warm readable soil and dark green foliage. Only river, bare dry ground, rocks, roots, conifers and hazy sky occupy the picture. Photoreal painterly documentary landscape, vertical composition, one warm copper sun accent.
options.art_direction: Unoccupied arid Early Triassic environment, rust-red mineral ground, subdued copper sunlight, nature-documentary landscape with readable soil texture.

options.label: Hollow in the dunes
options.vo: Dig into a hollow between dunes.
options.image_prompt: Unoccupied ground-focused natural-history view of a sheltered bowl-shaped depression between large smooth red sand dunes in an arid Early Triassic desert. Fine curved ripple lines cover the near sand. Rounded dune slopes enclose a small low hollow in the centre of the composition. The rim of the nearest dune creates a broad clean arc across the upper third. A little hazy copper sky is visible above that rim, with one restrained warm setting-sun glow at the right. Only loose red sand, subtle wind ripples, rounded dune slopes and a small strip of sky occupy the picture. Soft heat haze and long warm shadows reveal the hollow shape. premise.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 7, because extreme heat may have left Pangaea's tropics empty of land vertebrates. Your best bet is far south.

fact.text: After the Permian–Triassic extinction, extreme heat may have made Pangaea's low latitudes uninhabitable for tetrapods, the land vertebrates.
fact.source_sentence: A tetrapod gap may have existed from the Induan until the early Spathian between ~30 °N and ~ 40 °S due to extreme heat making these low latitudes uninhabitable for these animals.

premise.description: Just after the Great Dying, the middle of Pangaea got so hot that land animals may have vanished from it. Eight ways to beat the heat, and the long walk the evidence points to.
premise.related_topic_hint: Pangaea: One Night on Earth's Supercontinent

script: Pangaea's tropics are too hot to live in. Rest on a shady tropical riverbank. Float in a warm equator lagoon. Dig into a hollow between dunes. Hide in a cave in red cliffs. Chase the giant monsoon storms. Settle by a volcanic hot spring. Trek thousands of kilometres south. Cross the inland desert at noon. Real answer: number 7, because extreme heat may have left Pangaea's tropics empty of land vertebrates. Your best bet is far south. Comment your number.
